title: Launch: show the spec check's progress, say to wait for it, and keep raw report text out of the sitting
lead: *Proposed.* While the spec check runs after `l` (Waves and Roadmap launch), ork says what it is checking, how long it has run, and that the owner must wait for the confirmation. `ork run` and `ork wave start` print one line that says the same before they wait. The shared `Owner needed` text of a spec check no longer carries the role's prose after a `none`, or code fence lines, and the Waves list shows it on one line. The exact form of the progress, the confirm behaviour and the CLI line wait on the owner questions below; the steps are written for the recommended options.
findings_note: Owner 2026-11-03 (screenshots of a slicer wave launch): after l the Waves screen shows only 'pending: spec.check' in the footer, with no progress and no hint that the owner must wait for the spec check to finish before the confirm. Wanted: a spec check progress bar (items checked of ticked) and a plain line such as 'spec check: 2 of 4 items; wait, the launch confirm comes next'. Also seen in the same flow: the spec check sitting under Unplaced showed raw model text ('Owner needed: none', a stray code fence, and 'Reading the code closed these gaps. None needs an owner decision: - **s443:** ...', then '+13 more lines'), so the report's prose reached the sitting instead of only questions; cause not traced. Both the Waves screen and 'ork run' print the spec check state; check both. Related: S262 (jump to Running after launch), S258, S243.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** a per-item count that moves during the pass (Q1 option 3), a daemon progress message (Q1 option 2), a queued confirmation (Q3 option 2), changes to the spec-check prompt, ParseSpecCheck or its retry, the Running view jump after launch (S262), the report nudge of other roles (S243).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner report with screenshots, 2026-11-03, of a wave launch in the slicer project. After `l` on the Waves screen the status line read only `pending: spec.check`: no progress, and no hint that the confirmation comes after the check. The owner asked for a progress count such as `spec check: 2 of 4 items`. In the same flow the Waves list, under Unplaced, showed `Owner needed: none`, a stray code fence, prose that began `Reading the code closed these gaps. None needs an owner decision: - **s443:** ...`, and then `+13 more lines`.

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-03):

- Waves sets the status `pending: spec.check` once, when the check starts (`internal/tui/speccheck.go:92-93`), and clears it when the reply comes (`:111-112`). The Roadmap launch draws `pending: spec.check` in its body (`internal/tui/launch.go:491-492`), with an empty status line (`docs/dashboard.md:1481-1482`). Nothing records when the check started, so nothing can show elapsed time. While the check runs, `l` is refused with no text (`internal/tui/waves.go:359-361`), and ticking is off (`waves.go:392`). The confirmation is built only after the reply (`askLaunch`, `speccheck.go:148-167`).
- The TUI redraws every second: the poll tick runs at `TickEvery`, default one second (`internal/tui/model.go:214-216`, `:307-319`), and the harness clock is `h.now` (`internal/tui/tui_test.go:111-115`). So an elapsed time needs no new timer. The existing `elapsed` helper drops seconds after the first minute (`internal/tui/overview.go:1307-1320`).
- The daemon cannot count items done during the check. `spec.check` is one synchronous call (`internal/daemon/client.go:306-314`). The daemon answers cached items at once and runs one role pass over the stale ones (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:155-179`). That pass is one `Runner.Run` over the whole batch (`internal/engine/speccheck.go:209-245`), and the verdicts come only from the final report (`:291`, `:311`). So during the pass the daemon knows only: how many items were already cached, how many are in the pass, the attempt (one automatic retry, `:144-156`) and the vendor in the fallback chain (`:226-303`). One pass for the batch is the decided design (adj 164, `roles.spec-check`). The IPC layer can carry server notifications on a connection (`internal/ipc/ipc.go:374-409`), but `spec.check` sends none.
- Why the prose reached the screen. The engine takes the whole `## Owner needed` section: `section` reads every line after the heading up to the next `## ` heading or the end of the text (`internal/engine/report.go:283-298`). It drops the text only when the whole body is `none` (`isNone`, `report.go:302-306`; used at `internal/engine/speccheck.go:318-322`). The prompt says to end the report with `## Owner needed` and write `none` there (`internal/roles/prompts/spec-check.md`, Report section), and its examples are in a `text` code fence. A report that ends `none`, then a fence line, then prose keeps all of it as `OwnerNeeded`. The daemon passes it through and remembers it (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:187-193`, `:268`), also in `answers.json` (`:330`; loaded again at `internal/daemon/speccheck_state.go:105`). The Waves list prints it in full under the table, after Unplaced (`internal/tui/waves.go:812-814`), so the window cuts it with `+N more lines` (`internal/tui/view.go:938-941`). The sitting prints it too (`internal/tui/speccheck.go:376-379`), and so does the CLI (`internal/cli/wave.go:254-256`). The S143 review already noted that the Waves list can fold the whole text into `+N more lines` (S143 later note 2, 2026-10-28).
- Not verified: the report of that check itself. It lives under `~/.local/state/ork/spec-checks/` (`docs/design.md:776-780`), outside the workspace, and was not read. Whether the fence came from the role's report file or from the vendor's final text (`readSpecReport`, `internal/engine/speccheck.go:325-332`) is not known. The chain above holds for either.
- `ork run` and `ork wave start` print nothing between the plan and the spec check's reply (`internal/cli/wave.go:245-256`; `ork run` calls the same function, `internal/cli/run.go:132`).
- slicer has nothing like this. `slicer --root ../slicer find` for `progress`, `elapsed` and `spec check progress` finds only slicer's own status, stats and relay board items; `spec check` finds s392, s399 and s400 (the ledger roles, the answers path and the readiness record), none of which reports progress. The spec check job is ork's own (adj 164).

adj: `roles.spec-check` is decided (adj 164: one batch pass). `ui.wave-composer` is decided (adj 135) and is not changed. No record exists for `ui.spec-check`, `ui.spec-check-progress`, `ui.launch-progress` or `speccheck.progress` (`adj check`: not found).

This slice touches the UI (`internal/tui`, its golden views, `docs/dashboard.md`, `internal/cli` output), so rule u10 applies: it gets a UI pass (row r14) on every size.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Written for the recommended options. Run them first and see them fail. Below, FENCE stands for a line of three backticks, and FENCEtext for three backticks followed by `text`; write them in Go as string literals.

`internal/tui/speccheck_test.go`:

- TestSpecWaitText: `specWaitText([]string{"S90"}, 12*time.Second)` is `spec check: S90, 12s; wait for the confirmation`; `specWaitText([]string{"A", "B"}, 72*time.Second)` is `spec check: 2 items, 1m12s; wait for the confirmation`; three items at 3725 s give `spec check: 3 items, 1h02m; wait for the confirmation`. `checkClock(59*time.Second)` is `59s`, `checkClock(60*time.Second)` is `1m00s`, a negative duration is `0s`.
- TestWavesSpecCheckSaysToWaitWithItsElapsedTime: `wavesHarness`, `twoWaveItems`, then `_, cmd := h.m.Update(press("l"))` without delivering `cmd`. The view has `spec check: 2 items, 0s; wait for the confirmation` and no `pending: spec.check`. Set `h.now = h.now.Add(72 * time.Second)`: the view has `spec check: 2 items, 1m12s; wait for the confirmation`. Press `l` again: no second check call, no confirmation, the same text. Deliver `cmd()`: the confirmation `ork wave start ork A B? [y/N] (Enter is No)` shows and the wait text is gone.
- TestWavesSpecCheckShowsPendingAndBlocksTickAndLaunch (`:93`): expect the new text instead of `pending: spec.check`; the rest is unchanged.
- TestWavesListShowsOneLineOfOwnerNeeded: the check returns A and B ready and `OwnerNeeded` `Slice S2 could not be read.\nSecond line.\nThird line.`; press `n` at the confirmation. The view has `Owner needed: Slice S2 could not be read. (+2 more lines)` and no `Second line.`. At 80x24 the line is clipped to the body width and never wraps. A one-line text shows with no marker.
- TestWavesCheckingGolden: sizes 80x24 and 100x30, color and mono; `twoWaveItems`, `l` without delivering the check, `h.now` plus 72 s. Goldens `waves-checking-80x24-color.txt`, `waves-checking-80x24-mono.txt`, `waves-checking-100x30-color.txt`, `waves-checking-100x30-mono.txt`. The status line reads `spec check: 2 items, 1m12s; wait for the confirmation` on one line at both widths (51 characters; the Waves status has 58 columns at 80x24).

`internal/tui/launch_test.go`:

- TestLaunchSpecCheckSaysToWaitWithItsElapsedTime: `_, check := h.m.Update(launchPlanning(t, h)())`. The launch body has `spec check: S90, 0s; wait for the confirmation` exactly once, and `m.actionStatus` is empty. Plus 12 s: `spec check: S90, 12s; wait for the confirmation`. Deliver `check()`: the confirmation shows.
- TestLaunchRunsTheSpecCheckBeforeTheConfirmation (`:1053`) and TestLaunchStaleSpecCheckAfterNavigation (`:1241`): expect the new text instead of `pending: spec.check`.
- TestLaunchCheckingGolden: 80x24 and 100x30, color and mono, plus 72 s. Goldens `launch-checking-80x24-color.txt`, `launch-checking-80x24-mono.txt`, `launch-checking-100x30-color.txt`, `launch-checking-100x30-mono.txt`.

`internal/engine/speccheck_test.go`:

- TestSpecOwnerText, with lines joined by newlines: `none`, FENCE, an empty line, `Reading the code closed these gaps.` gives `""`. FENCEtext, `None.`, FENCE gives `""`. `Slice S2 could not be read.`, FENCE gives `Slice S2 could not be read.`. `Confirm the rollout window with the owner.` is unchanged. An empty body gives `""`.
- TestSpecOwnerNeededNoneWithTrailingTextIsNone: the runner's report is `specReport` with its `none` line under `## Owner needed` followed by FENCE, an empty line and `Reading the code closed these gaps. None needs an owner decision.` (the replace pattern of `TestOwnerNeededTextIsKept`, `:549-562`). `RunSpecCheck` returns `OwnerNeeded` `""`, and the saved `spec-check.md` still holds `Reading the code closed these gaps.`
- TestOwnerNeededTextIsKept (`:549`) stays green as it is.

`internal/daemon/speccheck_test.go`:

- TestStoredOwnerTextIsCleanedOnLoad: beside `TestOwnerAnswersSurviveARestart`; an `answers.json` whose fingerprint matches and whose `owner_needed` is `none`, FENCE, `prose` (newline-joined) loads; the next `spec.check` reply has an empty `owner_needed` and the item ready.

`internal/cli`:

- TestRunSaysToWaitForTheSpecCheck (`run_test.go`, beside `:750`): `singleSpecRun` with input `y` and a check reply where S1 is ready; stdout has the line `spec check: S1; wait for it to finish`, before `Start this slice?`. With `--json --yes` the line is on stderr and stdout is one JSON value.
- TestWaveStartSaysToWaitForTheSpecCheck (`wave_test.go`, beside `:251`): stdout has one line that starts `spec check: `, names S1 and S2, ends `; wait for it to finish`, and comes before `[S1 1/2]`.

The suite run decides which other CLI tests pin the exact output; fix each by expecting the new line.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Add the failing tests above. Run them and see the named failures.
2. `internal/tui/speccheck.go` (Q1): add `checkStarted time.Time` to `specState`. Add `checkClock(d time.Duration) string` (`0s` to `59s`, then `MmSSs`, then `HhMMm`; a negative duration is `0s`) and `specWaitText(items []string, d time.Duration) string`: one item names its id, more say `N items`, then `, CLOCK; wait for the confirmation`. Leave `elapsed` in `overview.go` as it is.
3. Waves (Q1, Q2, Q3): in `startSpecCheck` set `w.checkStarted = m.cfg.Now()` and no longer set `m.actionStatus`. In `view.go:102`, when the status is empty, the view is Waves and `m.waves.checking`, the status is `specWaitText` of the ticked ids and `m.cfg.Now().Sub(checkStarted)`. `waveLaunchRefusal` keeps refusing while checking (`waves.go:359-361`); no queued confirmation.
4. Roadmap launch (Q1, Q2): set `l.checkStarted = m.cfg.Now()` where the stage becomes `launchSpecPending` (`launch.go:295-297`), and draw `specWaitText([]string{l.params.Item}, ...)` in the body instead of `pending: spec.check` (`launch.go:491-492`). The status line stays empty.
5. `internal/engine/speccheck.go` (Q4): add `SpecOwnerText(body string) string`: drop every line whose trimmed text starts with three backticks, trim, and return `""` when the first non-blank line is none by `isNone`. Use it in place of `section` plus `isNone` at `:318-322`. The report file is saved before this, unchanged (`:315`).
6. `internal/daemon/speccheck_state.go:105` (Q4): pass a loaded `a.OwnerNeeded` through `engine.SpecOwnerText`, so an `answers.json` written before this slice no longer shows the prose. Do not rewrite the file.
7. `internal/tui/waves.go:812-814` (Q4): show only the first line of `w.ownerNeeded`, clipped to the body width with the existing `clip` helper, followed by ` (+N more lines)` when it has more lines. The sitting (`speccheck.go:376-379`) keeps the whole text.
8. `internal/cli/wave.go` (Q5): in `specCheck`, before the `spec.check` call, print `spec check: ID, ID; wait for it to finish` to the prompts writer `w`. `ork run` gets it through the same function.
9. Run `go test ./internal/tui -update` once, read the new golden files, and check that no existing golden changed. If one did, say which and why in the report.
10. Docs, as listed in Files. Mark the new texts *proposed*. Do not paste the relay contract's text.
11. Do not touch: the spec-check prompt (`internal/roles/prompts/spec-check.md`), `ParseSpecCheck`, the retry in `RunSpecCheck`, the daemon wire, or any slicer or adj data.
12. Add the CHANGELOG entry last, as the first item under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go test -race -count=1 -run 'Spec|Launch|Waves|Owner' ./internal/tui ./internal/engine ./internal/daemon ./internal/cli`.
- `rg -n "pending: spec.check" internal docs/dashboard.md` prints nothing.
- UI slice: UI pass (r14), rule u10. It changes `internal/tui`, its golden views, `docs/dashboard.md` and `internal/cli` output. Views to render: Waves while checking and the Roadmap launch while checking, at 80x24 and 100x30.
- [HUMAN CHECK] In the TUI, tick two items on Waves and press `l`: the status line reads `spec check: 2 items, Ns; wait for the confirmation` and the clock moves each second until the confirmation opens. On a check whose report ends with `none` and prose, the Waves list shows no `Owner needed` line.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Launch: say to wait for the spec check, with its elapsed time, and clean its Owner needed text".

sections.heading: Open owner questions
sections.body:
The owner has not answered these. Each names the steps that wait on it.

Q1. What is the progress? (waits: Implement steps 2, 3 and 4)
1. elapsed: the TUI shows the item count and the time since `l`, for example `spec check: 2 items, 1m12s; wait for the confirmation`. No daemon change. It is real but does not count items done.
2. phases: the daemon sends *proposed* `spec.progress` notifications on the `spec.check` connection: items already checked, items in this pass, attempt 1 or 2, vendor and model. The TUI shows `spec check: 2 of 4 already checked; checking 2 (claude sonnet), 40s`. The count does not move during the pass. Cost: a new wire message, a notification reader in the client and the TUI, CLI handling, daemon tests.
3. per item: one role pass for each item, so `2 of 4 items` moves. It goes against adj 164 (one pass), needs a new adj record, costs one role start for each item, and loses the shared question across slices.
Recommend 1: it is honest, small, and needs no wire change; option 2 can follow if the cached split proves useful.

Q2. Where is it shown? (waits: steps 3 and 4)
1. Where `pending: spec.check` is today: the Waves status line, and the Roadmap launch body.
2. Also a dim line in the Waves body above the table.
Recommend 1: one place for each view, and the status line is where the confirmation appears next.

Q3. What does `l` do while the check runs? (waits: step 3)
1. refused, with text: `l` stays refused and the status keeps the wait text; no confirmation until the reply.
2. queued: the y/N confirmation opens at once and says it starts after the check; `y` is held and applied when the reply is all ready; an item with questions still opens the sitting first.
Recommend 1: the confirmation must name the held items, and only the reply knows them.

Q4. How is the raw report text kept out? (waits: steps 5, 6 and 7)
1. both: the engine drops code fence lines from the Owner needed text and treats it as none when its first non-blank line is `none`; the Waves list shows only the first line, with `(+N more lines)`. The sitting and the CLI keep the whole cleaned text. The full report stays in `spec-check.md`.
2. engine only: clean the text, keep the Waves list as it is.
3. list only: show one line in the Waves list, keep the engine as it is.
Recommend 1: the engine fix removes this report's prose, and the one-line list keeps a real long text from pushing the table away (S143 later note 2).

Q5. What does the CLI print? (waits: step 8)
1. one line before the call, to the prompts writer (stdout, or stderr with `--json`): `spec check: S1, S2; wait for it to finish`.
2. that line, and on a terminal an elapsed line every 30 seconds.
Recommend 1: one line says it all, and a shell log stays short.
